document.title: U/S Pickering Discusses Afghanistan, Democratization and Kashmir in NY with [Excised] (State 221643)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Pakistan's Bin Laden Policy
document.note: [Confidential] Under Secretary Thomas Pickering meets Pakistani officials and expresses disappointment that Pakistan, a good friend of the U.S., was not helping with Usama bin Ladin. He rejects the claim that engagement is the only way to change Taliban behavior and says the U.S. will pursue harsher measures including sanctions, acting to protect U.S. interests at a time and place of its choosing. Excised.

persons.role: US Under Secretary of State for Political Affairs

THE U.S. WOULD ALWAYS ACT TO PROTECT U.S. INTERESTS AT A TIME AND PLACE OF ITS OWN CHOICE, PICKERING WARNED

events.description: Pickering meets Pakistani interlocutor in New York, presses on Afghanistan, UBL, USS Cole links, democratization and Kashmir.
USS Cole bombing; indications of connection to UBL.
Fall of Taloqan, which Pickering says Pakistan masterminded, sending tens of thousands of refugees fleeing.
Cable State 221643 sent to USUN reporting the meeting.
Under Secretary Pickering met a Pakistani official in New York, pressing on Taliban support, UBL/USS Cole link, democratization and Kashmir.
State Department cable 221643 reported on the meeting.
Bombing of the USS Cole, with indications of a connection to UBL.
Fall of Taloqan, sending tens of thousands of refugees fleeing; Pakistan closed its borders.
US, with Russia, pursued new UN sanctions and an arms embargo against the Taliban.

relationships.detail: UBL is in Taliban-held Afghanistan; Taliban claimed he was cut off from the outside world.
relationships.quote: DESPITE TALIBAN ASSURANCES THAT UBL WAS COMPLETELY CUT OFF FROM THE OUTSIDE WORLD

relationships.detail: UBL is under Taliban control/assurances in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: TALIBAN ASSURANCES THAT UBL WAS COMPLETELY CUT OFF FROM THE OUTSIDE WORLD

relationships.detail: Pickering cited mounting evidence of direct Pakistani involvement in the fighting in Afghanistan.
relationships.quote: MOUNTING EVIDENCE OF DIRECT PAKISTANI INVOLVEMENT IN THE FIGHTING IN AFGHANISTAN

relationships.detail: Pickering met a Pakistani interlocutor in New York on 14 Nov 2000.
relationships.quote: DURING A MEETING IN NEW YORK NOVEMBER 14

relationships.detail: UBL is the figure linked to the USS Cole attack; leadership of al-Qa'ida implied.
relationships.quote: INDICATIONS THAT THERE WAS A CONNECTION TO UBL

relationships.detail: Indications UBL was at least peripherally involved in the attack on the USS Cole.
relationships.quote: INDICATIONS THAT USAMA BIN LADIN (UBL) HAD BEEN AT LEAST PERIPHERALLY INVOLVED IN THE ATTACK ON THE USS COLE.

relationships.detail: Pickering is the Under-Secretary of State who classified the cable.
relationships.quote: CLASSIFIED BY UNDER-SECRETARY THOMAS R. PICKERING

relationships.detail: Cable signed ALBRIGHT as Secretary of State.
Pickering said the US had made numerous dialogue efforts with the Taliban, which persisted in misbehavior.
relationships.quote: WE HAVE HAD NUMEROUS EFFORTS OF DIALOGUE WITH THE TALIBAN

relationships.detail: US proposed an arms embargo and new sanctions against the Taliban.
relationships.quote: AN ARMS EMBARGO ON THE TALIBAN.

relationships.detail: Pakistan said the Taliban get their fuel from Central Asia, not Pakistan.
relationships.quote: THE TALIBAN GET THEIR FUEL FROM CENTRAL ASIA.

relationships.detail: Pickering claimed Pakistan masterminded the fall of Taloqan.
relationships.quote: THE FALL OF TALOQAN, WHICH PAKISTAN HAD MASTERMINDED

relationships.detail: Fall of Taloqan, attributed to Pakistani planning, generated refugees.
Security Council was considering new sanctions on the Taliban.
relationships.quote: THE SECURITY COUNCIL IMPOSED NEW SANCTIONS
THE CURRENT REGIME HAD HAD A DELETERIOUS EFFECT ON THE AFGHAN PEOPLE

key_claims: The US told Pakistan there was mounting evidence of direct Pakistani involvement in the fighting in Afghanistan.
The US saw indications that UBL was at least peripherally involved in the USS Cole attack despite Taliban assurances.
The US was considering an arms embargo on the Taliban and new sanctions with Russia.
Pickering claimed Pakistan masterminded the fall of Taloqan.
Pickering said Taliban encouraged opium poppy production and had previously taken aid money then expanded production.
The Pakistani interlocutor offered few facts and relied on a 'Pakistan as victim' argument.
